                                   ORDINANCE NO. 1659

         AN ORDINANCE APPROVING THE ALPINE HOLLOW DEVELOPMENT
         AGREEMENT FOR APPROXIMATELY 110 ACRES OF PROPERTY LOCATED AT
         APPROXIMATELY 3235 EAST 15780 SOUTH WITHIN DRAPER CITY.

       WHEREAS, the Land Use and Development Code of the Draper City Municipal Code
has been established to provide regulations concerning general developments within the
City Boundaries; and

      WHEREAS, the property is subject to the Suncrest Development Agreements, Suncrest
Design Guidelines and the 1999 Land Use and Development Code of the Draper City
Municipal Code; and

       WHEREAS, the City Council hereby determines that it will be in the best interest of the
City to allow development of the subject property in accordance with the Development
Agreement; and

       WHEREAS, the Development Agreement will allow for a wider roadway which will
benefit the City and future residents when it comes to safety, maintenance, repair,
emergency vehicle access, and snow removal; and

        WHEREAS, the Development Agreement will allow a maximum of 50 dwelling unit,
and requires all dwelling units to be fire sprinklered. This takes into account the number of
units allowed by the Suncrest Development Agreement and access roadway limitations; and

       WHEREAS, the proposed Development Agreement set forth herein has been reviewed
by the Planning Commission and the City Council, and all appropriate public hearings have
been held in accordance with Utah law to obtain public input regarding the proposed
modifications to development standards; and

        WHEREAS, the Planning Commission has reviewed and made a recommendation to
the City Council concerning the proposed Development Agreement, and the City Council has
found the proposed Development Agreement to be consistent with the City’s General Plan.

      NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF DRAPER CITY, STATE
OF UTAH:

      Section 1.  Development Agreement.       The City of Draper approves the
Development Agreement provided in Exhibit A, otherwise known as the Alpine Hollow
Development Agreement.

        Section 2.   Severability Clause. If any part or provision of this Ordinance is held

Ordinance No. 1659                            1                                      Alpine Hollow
                                                                             Development Agreement
invalid or unenforceable, such invalidity or unenforceability shall not affect any other portion
of this Ordinance and all provisions, clauses and words of this Ordinance shall be severable.

      Section 3.    Correction of Editing Errors. The city attorney is authorized to correct
any punctuation, spelling, formatting, clerical, or de minimis errors in Exhibit A prior to
submitting the ordinance for publishing.

        Section 4.   Effective Date. This Ordinance shall become effective immediately
upon publication or posting, or 30 days after final passage, whichever is closer to the date of
final passage.

PASSED AND ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF DRAPER CITY, STATE OF UTAH, ON THE
_____ DAY OF      , 2025.

                                            DRAPER CITY

                           DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT
                                 (Alpine Hollow)
        This Development Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into on the ____
 day of ____________, 2025, by and between The Ridges at Alpine, LLC, a
 Utah limited liability company ("Ridges") and Draper City ("City"), a Utah
 Municipal Corporation. Each of the Ridges and City are sometimes referred to
 herein as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties."

                                      RECITALS

      A. Ridges is the current owner of a 109.94 acre parcel of property located in Draper
         City, Utah County, Utah (Parcel No. 11:008:0012) and more particularly
         described on Exhibit A ("Property").

      B. In 2016 Draper City sold the Property to Blue Bison Development, LLC. As part
         of the sale, Draper City granted an access easement to the Property. Said
         easement begins at Suncrest Drive, and continues across other properties owned
         by Draper City to the west boundary of the Property as highlighted in green and
         set forth in Exhibit B. Ridges purchased the Property together with the access
         easement, from Blue Bison on April 2, 2024.

      C. In order to perfect the access easement granted by Draper City at the time of
         sale of the Property, a Cooperation Agreement (Metro Agreement) with
         Metro Water District of Salt Lake and Sandy (Metro Water) was required to
         cross over a fifty-foot wide parcel of land owned by Metro Water, as
         highlighted in pink and set forth in Exhibit C. City and Ridges are both
         parties to, and bound by the terms of said Cooperation Agreement with Metro
         Water found in Exhibit E.

      D. Ridges is also, under separate application, seeking approval from the City for
         the Alpine Hollow Subdivision Plat, consisting of 50 residential lots, for the
         development of the Ridges Property (the “Project”) in the general
         configuration highlighted in orange and set forth in Exhibit D.


                                            1
     E. The Suncrest Master Development Agreement (SMDA), along with the 1st and
        2nd Amendments to the agreement, governs the development of the Project.
        Ridges is seeking a modification to the road requirements under the SMDA, to
        increase the width of the roads in the Project.

     F. Ridges is also seeking modifications to the current Draper City Code to allow
        for a height increase of the fencing from 6 feet to 8 feet in height on the
        Project, and an increase to 12 feet in Height for the entrance feature columns
        and fencing.

     G. The City Council of Draper City (the “City Council”), acting pursuant to its authority
        under Utah Code § 10-9a-102(2) et seq., as amended, and Draper City Municipal
        Code (1999 DCMC _________________(the “City Code”), a copy of which is
        attached hereto and by this reference incorporated herein as Exhibit F and in
        furtherance of its land use policies, goals, objectives, ordinances, resolutions, and
        regulations, has elected to enter into this Agreement for the purpose of approving and
        regulating the development of the Project.

     H. The Parties believe that this Agreement will benefit the City by 1) Providing
        private access and project related roads requiring the Developer/HOA to assume
        the care, maintenance and repair of said roads, 2) The safety and welfare of
        the residents of Draper, who reside within the development will be improved
        by Developer installing wider roads than required by the SMDA, and 3)
        Effectuating access to this property by virtue of a Cooperation Agreement
        with Metro Water resolves any potential issues related to access under the
        sales agreements, and this Project brings the value of roads and infrastructure
        that aligns with the City masterplan.

     I. The City and Ridges intend for this Agreement to provide Ridges with vested
        entitlements for development of the Project. The City has determined that entering
        into this Agreement furthers the purposes of the Utah Municipal Land Use,
        Development, and Management Act, the City’s General Plan, and the City Code
        (collectively, the “Public Purposes”). As a result of such determination, the City has
        elected to move forward with the approvals necessary to approve the development of
        the Project in accordance with the terms and provisions of this Agreement. This
        Agreement is a “development agreement” within the meaning of and entered into
        pursuant to the terms of Utah Code Ann. §10-9a-102(2).

       NOW, THEREFORE, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and
sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

     1. Recitals; Definitions. The Recitals set forth above are incorporated herein by this
        reference. Any capitalized term used but not otherwise defined in this Agreement
                                            2
   shall have the meaning ascribed to such term in the City Code.

2. Restriction on the Development of the Ridges’ Property. Due to the unique
   nature, topography, slopes, location, access, design, and guidelines pertaining to the
   Project, the Parties have agreed to the following conditions:

      a. Compliance with Current City Ordinances. Unless specifically addressed
         in this Agreement, Ridges agrees that subdivision of the Project shall be
         developed in a manner that complies with applicable provisions of the SMDA
         and City Code (1999 version) as they exist on the date of execution of this
         Agreement. All other aspects of development and construction shall be
         governed by the current City Code.

      b. Density. A maximum number of Fifty (50) residential lots.

      c. Single-Family Residences and Out-Buildings. Except as otherwise
         stated, only single-family detached residential units may be constructed
         on the Lots. Pool houses, barns, casitas, mother-in-law apartments,
         detached garages and similar structures are permitted, so long as they
         are not used for rental space, the residential living space does not exceed
         3,000 square feet, and all residential living spaces are fire sprinkled.

      d. Setbacks. The lots shall be developed with standard SFD 35 front, side and
         rear yard setbacks as outlined in the [SMDA]Suncrest Development
         Guidelines Table 1.

      e. Public Utility Easements (“PUE”). All PUE’s are to be as presently depicted
         on the preliminary plat drawings. (“Preliminary Plat”) attached hereto as
         Exhibit G. Except for required stormwater drainage easements on specific
         lots and locations, all PUEs are located along the front property lines of the
         lots. All other side-yard and rear-yard protective PUEs listed in SMDA or
         Section 17-5-050(g) of the City Code are not required.

      f. Access and Subdivision Roads. The Parties acknowledge that the
         access road (“Access Road”) for the Project was granted at the time of
         sale of the Property in 2016. The Access Road begins at Suncrest Drive
         and ends at the west boundary of the Property and is labeled as “Alpine
         Peaks Way” as reflected on the Preliminary Plat. The Access Road is
         divided into two parts, namely the public section beginning at Suncrest
         Drive and ending just before the turn about immediately before the
         Entrance Gate to the Project as shown on the approved plat. From that
         point, the Access Road is a private easement extending to and

                                        3
   throughout the Project. The Developer is responsible for the installation
   of the improvements associated with the Access Road and subdivision
   roads as shown on the Preliminary Plat. Following completion of the
   Access Road and other subdivision roads improvements, the care,
   upkeep, repair, and maintenance of the public portion of the Access
   Road shall be the responsibility of the City, while the care, upkeep,
   repair, and maintenance, including snow removal, of the private section
   of the Access Road, subdivision roads and associated improvements
   (“Associated Improvements”) shall be the exclusive responsibility of the
   Developer and will ultimately be passed on to the Home Owner’s
   Association upon completion of the Project. The Associated
   Improvements, situated on City property and located both within and
   outside of the Access Road]-, include, the drainage facilities (inlets,
   culverts, structures, basins, and swales), cut and fill slopes together with
   the necessary retaining walls along the private section of the Access
   Road.

g. Width of Roads. The Parties acknowledge that the width of the Access
   Road and the subdivision roads in the Project were originally governed
   by the SMDA. The SMDA requires roads to be 30 feet in width, which
   has proven to be less than ideal over the years. The Ridges and City
   have mutually agreed that: (i) widening the Access Road and the
   subdivision roads is beneficial for the safety and welfare of the residents,
   as well as for ease of maintenance, repair, emergency vehicle access,
   snow removal, etc., and (ii) the width of the Access Road and the
   subdivision roads for the Project shall be increased to 56 feet in width,
   as reflected on the Preliminary Plat.

h. Site Fencing. A wrought iron fence of 6’ to 8’ in height will be required
   to be installed around the exterior perimeter of the Project for Property
   where residential lots exist.

   The City will not issue a building permit for construction on an exterior
   perimeter lot which borders City-owned Property unless and until a
   temporary chain link fence is installed along the rear Property line to
   protect from any encroachment upon or entering into the adjacent City-
   owned property. The City shall withhold a final certificate of occupancy
   until the lot owner for the subject lot installs the permanent wrought iron
   fencing along the exterior perimeter of the Lot.
                               4
   Lot owners shall ensure temporary chain link fencing or permanent
   wrought iron fencing is not installed within or upon any of the City-
   owned property. Lot owners shall further ensure that all temporary and
   permanent fencing is installed from the lot owner’s side of the property
   and that the fence installation company does not enter City-owned
   property without permission. Corner pins will be installed on each lot to
   mark the rear boundary of the lot. If the corner pins are disturbed or
   missing, the Lot owners will be required to hire a certified land surveyor
   to reinstall the pins and ensure this requirement is met. The City will
   verify the fencing location prior to issuance of building permit and
   issuance of certificate of occupancy.

   If fencing has been placed on the City-owned property, the lot owner
   shall remove the fencing and reinstall it on the lot boundary and shall
   prior to the issuance of a building permit or certificate of occupancy
   repair any damage to the City-owned property caused during
   construction on the lot.

i. Entrance Feature and Fencing Heights and Monument Sign. The
   Developer has submitted a drawing of the entrance gate and the guard
   building for the Project. The height of the gates, fencing, and entrance
   feature exceed the height allowed by ordinance, 1999 DCMC Section 9-
   3-090. The City acknowledges and agrees that given the location, scale
   of the entrance feature and its surroundings, a variation of 12 feet in
   height is appropriate and shall be allowed for the entrance feature area.
   The maximum height for the perimeter fencing for each lot on the
   Project is increased from 6-feet to 8-feet in height. The fencing across
   the bridge shall be as reflected on the plans. An entry monument and
   signage that complies with freestanding monument sign standards in
   City code is to be allowed on Suncrest Drive. A separate easement will
   be allowed for the sign.

j. Water System Maintenance. Maintenance of the water system will be the
   responsibility of the homeowners’ association.
         i.   Private Community Responsibilities.
              a. Post-Transfer Maintenance. Once the water system has been
                   completed and transferred, the homeowners’ association will
                   assume full responsibility for the ongoing maintenance, repairs,
                   and upgrades of the water infrastructure. This includes
                   ensuring compliance with water quality regulations, scheduling


                                 5
                         regular inspections, and promptly addressing any identified
                         issues to prevent risks to public health and safety.
                     b. Responsibility After City Water Meter. All water
                         infrastructure beyond the city water meter, including pipes and
                         connections on private property, is the responsibility of the
                         homeowners’ association. The City is responsible only for
                         infrastructure up to and including the water meter. Any issues
                         beyond the meter, such as leaks or contamination, fall under
                         the homeowners’ association responsibility.
                     c. Funding for Maintenance. The homeowners’ association will
                         establish and manage a maintenance fund to cover the costs
                         associated with the water system's upkeep. All residents will
                         contribute to this fund through assessments or fees as
                         determined by the homeowners’ association.
                     d. Third-Party Services. The homeowners’ association may hire
                         licensed third-party contractors for specialized maintenance
                         and repairs as needed. The homeowners’ association will
                         oversee these contracts and ensure contractors comply with all
                         relevant water safety standards.
               ii.   City Oversight and Intervention. The City reserves the right to
                     intervene if the homeowners’ association fails to maintain the
                     water system in a manner that ensures the health and safety of the
                     public. If the City determines that the water infrastructure poses a
                     risk to public health, it may step in to correct deficiencies at the
                     homeowners’ association expense. Ridges grants to the City an
                     express right of entry in order to correct such deficiencies that are
                     contemplated by this section. Additionally, the City has the
                     authority to conduct routine flushing, water quality sampling, and
                     other necessary testing to ensure compliance with health standards.
                     However, the City is not responsible for any infrastructure failures,
                     damages, or disruptions resulting from these activities or from
                     issues within the private water system.

      k. Side Lot Lines. The development plans include some lots with side lot lines
         that are not located at right angles to the roadway or radial to roadway curves
         as required by DCMC. This is a result of the unique topography of the site.
         The City agrees that the lots as designed provide for an adequate buildable
         width and building envelope that may not otherwise be achievable if the side
         lot lines were at right angles and radial.

3. Metro Water District Contract – Party Responsibility and Survival. A copy of
   the Cooperation Agreement for Non-District Use of District Lands and Interest in

                                       6
   Lands (Metro Agreement) is attached hereto and incorporated by reference herein as
   Exhibit E.
      a. The Metro Agreement is specific in its terms and conditions and the specific
          responsibilities of Ridges and City, respectively.
      b. The foregoing notwithstanding, it is expressly understood that:
               i. Ridges is solely responsible for the installation of the entire Access
                  Road, utilities and all other improvements.
              ii. Ridges, its successors and assigns are solely responsible for the
                  maintenance, repair, upkeep, snow removal and all other costs
                  associated with the private section of the Access Road as more fully
                  defined on the Alpine Peaks Way Dedication Plat – Exhibit B.
             iii. Ridges (not the City) is responsible to reimburse Metro Water for
                  costs pursuant to the Metro Agreement, unless said costs are a result
                  of the City’s failure to perform its exclusive responsibilities under the
                  Metro Agreement.
      c. The obligations of each Party under the Metro Agreement are and shall
          remain an essential term of this Agreement. Each Party’s performance under
          the Metro Agreement shall survive any termination or expiration of this
          Agreement and shall run with the land.


4. Limitation and No Guarantee. Ridges acknowledges that the development of the
   maximum number of lots (50), and every other aspect of the development of the
   Ridges Property requires that each development application, including each
   residential building permit application, comply with the City Code including,
   without limitation, the City's geologic hazards requirements. Subject to Section 8,
   the City's entry into this Agreement does not guarantee that Ridges will be able to
   construct the maximum number of homes or any other aspect of the Ridges Property
   until and unless it has complied with all the applicable requirements of the City Code.

5. Access to City Trails. Ridges hereby conveys to the City right-of-entry on the
   private portion of the Access Road as well as any other private roads necessary in
   the development for the express purpose of emergency service access and for
   servicing and maintaining any City-owned trails or trail infrastructure as identified
   in the attached Exhibit H. Such right-of-entry shall not be construed to mean public
   access. This section shall not be construed to grant access for construction of new
   trails.

6. Time Frame for Performance and Time Limitation. This Agreement will be
   binding on Ridges and its successors and assigns in perpetuity unless this Agreement
   is modified in accordance with the provisions of the Agreement outlined below or
   until buildout, which shall be the completion of all of the development on the entire
   Property in accordance with the approved plans. As time is of the essence, the City

                                         7
   agrees to expedite necessary reviews, comments, and approvals. The City will allow
   applicable applications to be submitted simultaneously and run concurrently for all
   approvals.


7. Description of City Approvals. Preliminary Plat [attached as Exhibit G] approval
   shall run concurrently with approval and execution of this Agreement. The following
   additional City approvals will be required through the City staff, before the
   commencement of construction of improvements on the Property may begin:

        a.     Final Plat Approval
        b.     Subdivision Land Disturbance Permit Approvals
        c.     Applicable Bonds (Public Roadway and culinary water system)
        d.     Applicable Pre-Construction Meetings

8. Enforcement. The City may enforce the terms and conditions of this Agreement by
   refusing to issue a building permit for any construction that would be in violation of
   the development limitations set forth herein. This section shall in no way limit the
   City’s ability to enforce its ordinances through withholding a certificate of
   occupancy.

9. Governing Law. This Agreement shall be construed and enforced in accordance
   with the laws of the State of Utah.


10. No Modification. This Agreement may not be amended or modified except in
   writing executed by the Party against whom such amendment or modification is
   being charged and recorded in the official records.


11. Vested Rights. To the maximum extent permissible under the laws of Utah and the
   United States and at equity, the City and Ridges intend that this Agreement grants
   Ridges all rights to develop the Property and Project in fulfillment of this Agreement
   except as specifically provided herein.


12. Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the
   Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior
   agreements with respect thereto, whether oral or written.

13. No Waiver. No delay or omission in exercising any right or in enforcing any
   provision of this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of such right or
   provision. Failure of any Party hereto to exercise any right hereunder shall
   not be deemed a waiver of any such right and shall not affect the right of

                                         8
   such party to exercise at some future date any such right or any other right
   it may have.

14. Mutual Drafting. This Agreement is the result of mutual negotiation and
   drafting by both Parties. No provision of this Agreement shall be construed
   against either Party on the basis that one Party was the primary drafter.

15. Limitation on Recovery for Default - No Damages. The terms and
   conditions of this Agreement notwithstanding, no Party shall be entitled to any
   claim for monetary damages as a result of any breach of this Agreement and
   each Party waives any claims thereto. The sole remedy available to Ridges (or
   any assign or purchaser of a portion of the Property) or the City shall be that of
   specific performance. Both Parties waive any claim for costs or attorneys' fees
   incurred in connection with any litigation associated with this Agreement.

16. No Third-Party Rights/No Joint Venture. This Agreement does not create a
   joint venture relationship, partnership or agency relationship between the City
   and Ridges. Further, the Parties do not intend this Agreement to create any
   third-party beneficiary rights.

17. Assignability. The rights and responsibilities of Ridges under this Agreement
   may be assigned in whole or in part by Ridges with the consent of the City as
   provided herein.

       a. Ridges shall give Notice to the City of any proposed assignment and
          provide such information regarding the proposed assignee that the City
          may reasonably request in making the evaluation permitted under this
          Section. Such Notice shall include providing the City with all necessary
          contact information for the proposed assignee.

       b. Unless the City objects in writing within thirty (30) calendar days of
          notice, the City shall be deemed to have approved of and consented to the
          assignment.

       c. If any proposed assignment is for less than all of Ridges' rights and
          responsibilities then the assignee shall be responsible for the performance
          of each of the obligations contained in this Agreement to which the
          assignee succeeds.



                                       9
            d. The City may only withhold its consent if the City is not reasonably
               satisfied of the assignee's financial ability to perform the obligations of
               Ridges or there is an existing breach of a development obligation owed to
               the City by the assignee or related entity that has not either been cured or
               in the process of being cured in a manner acceptable to the City.

            e. Any assignee shall consent in writing to be bound by the assigned
               terms and conditions of this Agreement as a condition precedent to
               the effectiveness of the assignment.

            f. The foregoing notwithstanding, Ridges's selling or conveying lots, in any
               approved phase of the project, to builders, private lot owners, or sub-
               developers, shall not be deemed to be an "assignment" subject to the
               above- referenced approval by the City.

     18. Binding Effect. If Ridges sells or conveys lots to builders, private lot
        owners or subdividers, the lots so sold and conveyed shall be subject to this
        Agreement.

     19. Recordation and Running with the Land. This Agreement shall be
        recorded in the chain of title for the Ridges Property. This Agreement shall
        be deemed to run with the land.

     20. Binding Agreement. Each Party represents and warrants that this
        Agreement has been duly and validly authorized, executed and delivered,
        and constitutes the valid and binding obligation of such Party, and is
        enforceable in accordance with its terms.

     21. Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in multiple counterparts,
        each of which shall, for all purposes, be deemed an original and all of which,
        taken together, shall constitute one and the same agreement.

        IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of
the date first set forth above.
